newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity makes fund manager changes.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity makes fund manager changes.

text.p: Fidelity Investments on Tuesday named several fund managers to replace Larry Greenberg and Andrew Offit, both of whom departed the mutual fund company to join other firms.
Steven Wymer, manager of the $2.1 billion Fidelity Dividend Growth Fund, was named manager of the $9.6 billion Fidelity Growth Company Fund, Fidelity said.
John Hurley, manager of the $428 million Fidelity Select Software and Computer Services Fund, was named to head the $1.9 billion Fidelity Emerging Growth Fund, Fidelity said.

Jennifer Uhrig, manager of Fidelity Advisor Mid-Cap Stock Fund and the $1.7 billion Fidelity Mid-Cap Stock Fund, was named manager of the $6.2 billion Fidelity Variable Insurance Products (VIP) Fund: Growth Portfolio and the $2.5 billion Fidelity Advisor Equity Growth Fund.

The more than a dozen managerial changes included research analysts becoming portfolio managers, Fidelity spokeswoman Teri Kilduff told Reuters. "We always keep talking about the strength of the bench and this is what you're going to see," she said. "This is the new generation of Fidelity managers that have been developed through the Fidelity system."

Greenberg was considered among Fidelity's top managers, heading four funds: Growth Company Fund, Emerging Growth Fund, Advisor Equity Growth Fund and VIP Growth Fund, with combined assets of more than $21 billion under management.
His loss was considered a blow to Fidelity and spurred the series of changes, fund analysts said.
Among the other changes, Charles Mangum was named portfolio manager of Fidelity Dividend Growth Fund, succeeding Wymer. Mangum previously managed Fidelity OTC Portfolio since June 1996.
Robert Bertelson was named portfolio manager of Fidelity OTC Portfolio, succeeding Mangum. Bertelson previously managed Fidelity Convertible Securities Fund since June 1996.

Katherine Collins was named portfolio manager of Fidelity Mid-Cap Stock Fund and Fidelity Advisor Mid-Cap Fund, succeeding Uhrig. Collins previously managed Fidelity Select Consumer Industries Portfolio, Fidelity Advisor Consumer Industries Fund and Fidelity Select Leisure Portfolio.

A number of Fidelity's Select sector funds also changed hands, including the Fidelity Select Software and Computer Services Portfolio, Fidelity Select Leisure Portfolio, Fidelity Select Consumer Industries Portfolio and Fidelity Select Energy Portfolio among others.
